chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to go to the Masjid early on Friday when the sun was at the height of a spear's shadow. And when it was the month of Ramadan, he would go before that. And he (peace be upon him) used to say: 'The Fridays of the month of Ramadan have a merit over the Fridays of the other months just as the month of Ramadan has a merit over the other months.'

key_terms.قَدْرَ رُمْحٍ: The height of a spear's shadow (a specific time indicator)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Friday prayers during Ramadan according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Imam’s (peace be upon him) emphasis on *taqdim* (early arrival) for Friday prayers, a practice intensified in Ramadan to maximize spiritual reward. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the multiplicative merit of Ramadan elevates its Fridays, reflecting the broader theological principle that time itself is sanctified by divine decree. This practice serves as a practical model for believers to align their daily routines with the heightened spiritual atmosphere of the holy month.
